description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) while probing signal handlers.  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/probes/forkpid.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main:

    my $parent = $$; my $p = fork(); if (!$p) { print $$ == $parent ? "STALE" : "fresh"; exit }
        perl: fresh          PCL: STALE        (getppid() in the child is right in both)

perl refreshes `$$` in the child after every fork.  PCL evidently reads the pid once.  Fix shape: `$$` reads getpid() at use (a syscall is ~100 ns; or refresh the cached value inside p-fork's child branch -- and in the child side of `open "-|"` / `open "|-"` forks and IPC::Open2/3's).  Guard: a fork row in an existing process-tests file; probe `$$` inside a piped-open child too.
ALSO MEASURED THERE (file separately if not already known -- grep first): %SIG handlers are installed only for SOME signals.  probes/sig2.pl (parent signals a child that set `$SIG{NAME} = sub {...}`): perl handles INT TERM HUP USR1 USR2 PIPE WINCH; under PCL the child is KILLED by HUP (signal 1) and USR1 (10) -- the handler was never installed -- and the INT/TERM children print nothing; the run hung at USR2 (timeout).  `$SIG{HUP}` (daemon reload) and `$SIG{USR1}` are everyday.  ALRM: handler runs but `sleep` is not interrupted (#2002).


=== HALF DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
`$$` is FIXED: `p-fork` refreshes it in the child branch, which is what the
pipe-open fork already did.  forkpid.pl identical to perl (child fresh, parent
unchanged, piped child fresh).  Guard: one row in Pl/t/system-block-01.t,
inverse-verified.

THE SECOND HALF IS UNTOUCHED AND THIS TASK STAYS OPEN FOR IT: %SIG handlers
are installed for SIGALRM ONLY.  `%p-ensure-alarm-handler` is the single
`sb-sys:enable-interrupt` site in the whole runtime (grep confirms), so
`$SIG{HUP}`, `$SIG{USR1}`, `$SIG{TERM}`, `$SIG{INT}`, `$SIG{CHLD}` and the
rest are never installed and the child is killed by the default disposition.
`$SIG{HUP}` (daemon reload) and `$SIG{USR1}` are everyday.

FIX SHAPE, with what s492c learned: the handler must be installed LAZILY, when
`%SIG{NAME}` is assigned a code ref (an eager loop over 30 signals at startup
would change the disposition of every program), and the trampoline is the one
ALRM already uses -- including its new `*p-sleep-wakeup*` throw (task #2002),
so that a TERM handler ends a `sleep 60` the way perl's does.  `%SIG` is a
plain hash today, so catching the assignment needs either a tie/magic cell or
a check at the points that read it.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 5 (0e6014eb).  p-fork refreshes $$ in the child branch,
which is what the pipe-open fork already did.  Normative statement:
docs/ir-spec.md 8, the `$$` row.  Guard: one of the five rows added to
Pl/t/system-block-01.t.  The %SIG half of this task (HUP / USR1 handlers never
installed) is #2107's, not this one's.



=== DONE (s494g) -- the %SIG half ===
The second half (HUP / USR1 / TERM / INT / CHLD handlers never installed) SHIPPED with #2107 (s494g, 2026-09-25): every program-ownable signal's handler is installed at the %SIG store, a handler that returns ends a running `sleep` (#2002's wakeup), and probes/sig2.pl's shape (parent signals a child that set $SIG{NAME}) is perl-identical for INT TERM HUP USR1 QUIT WINCH (q5 battery, scratch/s494g/battery-after-final.log).  USR2 is the one exception: SBCL's GC stop signal, derived as runtime-owned at boot, announced and not installed (not-supported.md "%SIG").
subject: SILENT WRONG (dangerous): `$$` is STALE in a forked child -- it still holds the PARENT's pid, so `kill SIG, $$` in a child signals the parent, and "/tmp/x.$$" collides between parent and child
